title: The editing checklist.
lines: Read your draft aloud quietly to yourself.
Then check each point below:
•  Does the rhetorical question open the piece?
•  Is the present tense used consistently throughout?
•  Does each skill section explain WHAT, HOW and WHY?
•  Have you used at least three different connectives?
•  Is the register formal? (No chatty phrases or ‘you should’)
•  Does the conclusion link the skills together?
Make corrections in a different colour.
Aim to improve at least two things before the partner share.

lines: Peer reading.
Swap drafts with your partner.
Read their explanation text carefully.
Give two specific pieces of feedback:
●  One strength: what does their text do well?
Be specific — quote the sentence or connective.
●  One suggestion: where could they explain HOW or WHY
more clearly, or use a different connective?
Then make any final improvements to your own draft.

title: Sharing our writing.
lines: Two or three writers will read their explanation text aloud.
As you listen, think about:
•  Which rhetorical question was the most effective?
•  Which skill section explained HOW and WHY most clearly?
•  Which connective use sounded the most natural?
Return to the key question:
How does a writer make a reader feel characters’ emotions?
How does the explanation text answer this question in a different way
to the narrative you wrote in weeks one and two?

q1: What is the most important thing you changed when you edited your draft?
q2: How is explaining something in writing different from just describing it?
q3: Looking at both your narrative and your explanation text, which do you think shows your best writing this term?
